title: TouchLine Matchday Ledger
description: A football working interface built from fixture-sheet rhythm, score columns and a structural touchline rule.

fontFamilies.product: Sora, Segoe UI, system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, sans-serif

typographyMeta.figures: Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for scores, clocks, tables, ratings and records.
typographyMeta.case: Use sentence case. Capitals are reserved for codes, metadata labels, table headers and match states.
typographyMeta.measure: Keep explanatory text to a readable narrow measure even when the game workspace is wide.

narrative.overview: TouchLine is a football game, not a SaaS dashboard. The interface is a modern matchday working document: calm enough to make decisions in, quick enough to scan during a match, and dramatic only when football supplies the event. The same system covers Home, setup, draft, the Dugout, matchday, summaries and utility screens in Floodlit and Daylight themes.
narrative.creativeNorthStar: The Matchday Ledger. Every screen should feel like one page of the same football run: choose, draft, prepare, play, review. Fixture-sheet rhythm, aligned figures and one structural touchline rule create hierarchy without interchangeable rounded cards. Cover the logo and the interface should still read as TouchLine.
keyCharacteristics: Cool match paper by day and stadium blue by night
Score-led Sora typography with tabular figures
Hairline rules and restrained surfaces instead of a card cloud
One structural touchline rule across navigation, headings and chronology
Quiet routine motion with expressive football events
rules: Normal content is flat; depth belongs to overlays.
Pills are reserved for filters and true status.
Pages and lists do not run generic entrance cascades.
Hover movement is gated to fine pointers.
Visual work never changes deterministic engine behaviour or save compatibility.
dos: Lead with the next football decision, current score or competition state.
Let real data, badges, pitch diagrams and aligned figures carry the screen.
Use rules, whitespace and type before adding another container.
Reserve expressive motion for reveals, goals, results and trophies.
donts: Build a cloud of equal rounded cards.
Add decorative mode numbers, eyebrow copy above every heading or invented proof.
Use gradients, glows, glass or continuous motion on ordinary controls.
Hide a phone action behind an overlay or let sticky hover follow a touch.
